content.text:
The data was successfully retrieved from the ECB SDMX API. Here are the annual **Consumption of Fixed Capital (CFC)** values for **Georgia** from 1996 to 2023, denominated in **domestic currency (Georgian Lari, GEL)** at **current prices**:

| Year | CFC (GEL) |
|------|-----------|
| 1996 | 304,515,091.76 |
| 1997 | 383,641,663.61 |
| 1998 | 516,397,121.22 |
| 1999 | 661,603,834.43 |
| 2000 | 631,701,000.89 |
| 2001 | 706,983,726.79 |
| 2002 | 790,112,565.20 |
| 2003 | 932,916,219.67 |
| 2004 | 976,818,537.80 |
| 2005 | 1,113,450,058.59 |
| 2006 | 1,306,373,084.13 |
| 2007 | 1,617,029,966.26 |
| 2008 | 1,758,049,267.67 |

| 2010 | 2,046,413,234.67 |
| 2011 | 2,350,512,405.91 |
| 2012 | 2,643,602,887.97 |
| 2013 | 1,555,932,152.32 |
| 2014 | 2,984,890,468.69 |
| 2015 | 3,657,280,672.54 |
| 2016 | 4,004,828,719.85 |
| 2017 | 4,492,921,334.91 |
| 2018 | 4,843,616,440.29 |
| 2019 | 5,452,957,379.35 |
| 2020 | 6,152,769,261.62 |
| 2021 | 7,072,625,348.90 |
| 2022 | 7,661,448,474.88 |
| 2023 | 9,410,657,843.71 |

**Data details:**
- **Series**: `IDCM.A.N.GE.W2.S1.S1.D.P51C.N1G._T._Z.XDC.V.N`
- **Indicator**: Consumption of fixed capital (P51C)
- **Country**: Georgia (GE)
- **Sector**: Total economy (S1)
- **Asset type**: Produced non-financial assets, gross (N1G)
- **Unit**: Domestic currency -- Georgian Lari (XDC), current prices
- **Frequency**: Annual
- **Observation status**: All values marked "A" (normal/acceptable)
- **Source**: ECB Statistical Data Warehouse (IDCM dataset)

**Notable observations:**
- CFC grew from roughly 305 million GEL in 1996 to over 9.4 billion GEL in 2023, reflecting roughly a 31-fold increase over the period.
- There is a notable dip in 2013 (1.56 billion GEL, down from 2.64 billion in 2012), which likely reflects a methodological revision or rebasing rather than an actual decline of that magnitude. The series then jumps to 2.98 billion in 2014.
- The 2009 value shows a slight decline from 2008, consistent with the global financial crisis impact.
- Growth has been particularly strong in recent years, with CFC increasing from 7.66 billion GEL in 2022 to 9.41 billion GEL in 2023 (a ~23% year-over-year increase).
